name: Maximize marketing campaign revenue under fixed budget

description: Baseline prefix-greedy revenue-per-spend heuristic from optimise.py.

asi.hypothesis: Establish the current revenue baseline before trying stronger selection algorithms.
asi.workload_shape: 62 campaign segments, 30M budget cap, current logic takes only the feasible prefix after ratio sort.
asi.known_weakness: If a high-ranked segment would overflow budget, later feasible segments are never considered.

description: Replace prefix-greedy selection with exact branch-and-bound knapsack search and expose budget usage metrics.

asi.hypothesis: An exact 0/1 knapsack search should beat the prefix heuristic because the dataset is small enough for aggressive pruning.
asi.algorithm: Branch-and-bound over revenue/spend-sorted segments using a fractional-knapsack upper bound and greedy seed lower bound.
asi.result_summary: Revenue increased by about 2.247M while nearly saturating the 30M budget.
asi.selection_behavior: Exact search still chooses 48 segments but replaces lower-value prefix choices with later feasible segments.

description: Tried pruning individually dominated rows before exact search to shrink the candidate set.

asi.hypothesis: Rows dominated by another row on spend and revenue might be removable without changing the optimal solution.
asi.rollback_reason: The 'dominated row' heuristic is invalid for 0/1 knapsack because the dominating row may already be selected; removing the dominated row can delete a legitimately useful second item and sharply reduce the optimum.
asi.next_action_hint: Avoid single-item dominance pruning unless multiplicity/capacity arguments make it safe; focus on search-ordering, bounds, or exact formulations instead.
asi.failure_mode: Revenue collapsed to 95.9106M with 1.904M budget slack, confirming the preprocessing removed useful combinable items.
asi.knapsack_lesson: Pairwise dominance is safe in fractional/unbounded settings more often than in this 0/1 single-copy setting.

description: Tried replacing branch-and-bound with exact Pareto-frontier dynamic programming using bitmask reconstruction.

asi.hypothesis: A Pareto-frontier DP might provide a cleaner exact solver while preserving the optimum.
asi.rollback_reason: It matched the current best revenue exactly but did not improve the primary metric, and benchmark time was not meaningfully better.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing branch-and-bound solver unless a future requirement favors clearer exact-state reconstruction over current code shape.
asi.result_equivalence: The DP frontier reached the same unique optimum 110.1627M with the same spend/slack profile.
asi.search_space_observation: An exploratory script showed only about 14.7k nondominated frontier states, so exact DP is feasible if maintainability becomes more important than pure minimal code.

description: Tried converting spend accounting to integer cents to make the exact search more numerically explicit.

asi.hypothesis: Representing budget and spend in integer cents may make the exact solver more robust without changing the optimum.
asi.rollback_reason: The result was identical on the benchmark and did not improve the primary metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler float-based implementation unless future datasets expose numerical precision problems or require audit-grade cent accounting.
asi.result_equivalence: Cent-based accounting reproduced the same 110.1627M optimum and 0.0015M budget slack.
asi.robustness_note: This is a viable hardening change, but not worth extra code under the current primary-metric-only objective.

name: Maximize marketing campaign revenue under budget and CS capacity limits

description: Reformulate the problem with budget, CS-contact, and contact-rate constraints and solve it exactly via SciPy MILP, with a pure-Python branch-and-bound fallback.

asi.hypothesis: Because the new CS constraints are linear, an exact MILP should preserve simplicity and solve much faster than extending the custom branch-and-bound by hand.
asi.solver_choice: scipy.optimize.milp via HiGHS returns the exact optimum in about 0.01s on the 62-row dataset.
asi.result_summary: Feasible optimum revenue is 109.8699M with spend 29.9981M, 3218 CS contacts, and 3.7650% contact rate.
asi.fallback_note: Retained a pure-Python multi-constraint branch-and-bound fallback for environments without SciPy.

description: Simplify the constrained solver to a direct SciPy MILP implementation with no custom branch-and-bound fallback.

asi.hypothesis: Because HiGHS already solves the exact three-constraint binary program instantly, deleting the fallback search should preserve the optimum while making the code smaller and slightly faster.
asi.simplification: Removed the revenue-density sorting and pure-Python fallback; solve the original dataframe directly with one MILP call.
asi.result_equivalence: The selected plan and all business metrics were unchanged at 109.8699M revenue, 3218 CS contacts, and 3.7650% contact rate.
asi.maintainability_gain: Code size dropped substantially and the benchmark script runtime fell from about 1.1s to about 0.7s without any objective regression.

description: Tried making the MILP objective use integer revenue cents instead of float revenue coefficients.

asi.hypothesis: Using integer revenue cents in the objective may make the exact optimization more explicit and avoid any solver tie ambiguity from floating-point coefficients.
asi.rollback_reason: It produced the identical optimum and did not improve the primary metric or meaningfully simplify the code.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the simpler float-coefficient MILP unless future datasets expose numerical edge cases or audit requirements around cent-level determinism.
asi.result_equivalence: Selection and all reported business metrics were unchanged, reinforcing that the current optimum is stable.
asi.robustness_note: Integer-cents objective remains a viable hardening tweak, but it is not worth extra code under the current objective.

description: Replace the tiny pandas path with csv.DictReader plus NumPy arrays while keeping the exact SciPy MILP solver.

asi.hypothesis: The dataset is small enough that pandas adds avoidable overhead; using csv + NumPy should keep the exact optimum while trimming code and runtime.
asi.simplification: Dropped DataFrame creation and computed all totals directly from NumPy arrays indexed by the MILP selection mask.
asi.result_equivalence: Business outputs stayed identical at 109.8699M revenue, 3218 CS contacts, and 3.7650% contact rate.
asi.runtime_note: End-to-end benchmark time improved again from about 0.7s to about 0.5s while preserving the exact same plan.
